vp.rule: free text stored raw; pre-step normalize (markdown, whitespace, curly apostrophes); the deterministic rule codes only clear replies: unanswered -> None; an explicit answer cue (the answer is / final answer / correct answer: / answer:) settles it, cues of two codes -> needs_coder; else all answer tokens of one code -> that code, tokens of two codes -> needs_coder (never guessed); a one-code reply is definite only if it has no attribution/foil frame (say, think, trap, trick, seems, people, most, irrelevant, doesn't apply ...; Numerical CRT also arithmetic words: less, half, before ...), at most 4 content words (function words and the item's own words not counted) and no word near a key of another code (one edit, about two for keys of 6+ letters); else needs_coder. Yes/no answers count only as the first word, not in idioms (no longer, no doubt, of course not). No token: a reply that is wholly a don't-know expression -> other, any other worded reply -> needs_coder, no word and no digit -> uncoded. Tokens ignore negated mentions, restatements of the question and discourse 'first'; keywords tolerate one-letter typos (real words excluded, vendored list sourcetext/realwords.txt)

rubric.categories: correct = the item's correct answer (or its trick recognised: no stairs, no smoke, he is dead ...); intuitive = the printed intuitive answer; other = any other wrong answer or 'I don't know' (codebook 3 'other incorrect answers'); uncoded = uninterpretable
